facts.text: A state is formed by the collective union of various districts.
facts.quote: A state is formed by the collective union of various districts.

facts.text: A district's own administrative machinery is called District Administration; it is a crucial link between State Administration and Local Self-Government bodies.
facts.quote: A district possesses its own distinct administrative machinery, which is known as District Administration. ... District Administration serves as a crucial link between State Administration and Local Self-Government bodies.

facts.text: District Administration handles revenue collection, agricultural irrigation, public welfare, disaster management, rationing, elections and supervising Local Self-Government bodies.
facts.quote: Responsibilities of the District Administration include functions such as revenue collection, agricultural irrigation, public welfare activities, disaster management operations, distribution of essential commodities (rationing), organization of elections and supervising the functioning of Local Self-Government bodies.

facts.text: The District Collector is the head of the District Administration.
facts.quote: District Collector is the head of the District Administration.

facts.text: The district is like a large ship, and the District Collector is its 'Captain'.
facts.quote: Our district is, in essence, this very 'ship' and the District Collector is its 'Captain'!

facts.text: Under the District Collector and District Magistrate come the Revenue Department (Deputy Collector, Tehsildar), Police Administration (Superintendent of Police) and Judicial Administration (District and Sessions Judge).
facts.quote: District Collector and District Magistrate ... Revenue Department ... Police Administration ... Judicial Administration ... Deputy Collector ... Tehsildar ... Superintendent of Police ... District and Sessions Judge

facts.text: A photo shows the District Collector Office, Sangli.
facts.quote: District Collector Office, Sangli

facts.text: District Revenue Machinery handles land administration, revenue, law and order, citizen services and natural disaster management and relief.
facts.quote: This administrative machinery handles crucial responsibilities such as land administration, revenue management, law and order, citizen services and natural disaster management and relief operations.

facts.text: Revenue structure: District Collector (chief revenue officer of district), Deputy Collector (assists Collector), Tehsildar (chief revenue officer of Taluka), Naib Tehsildar (assists Tehsildar), Mandal Officer (cluster of villages), Talathi (revenue officer of a village), Kotwal (assists Talathi).
facts.quote: 1. District Collector Chief Revenue Officer of the district. 2. Deputy Collector Assists the District Collector. 3. Tehsildar Chief Revenue Officer of the Taluka. 4. Naib Tehsildar Assists the Tehsildar. 5. Mandal Officer / Mandal Inspector Supervises a cluster of several villages. 6. Talathi Revenue Officer of a village. 7. Kotwal Assists the Talathi.

facts.text: The District Collector is an IAS officer, selected by the UPSC and appointed by the State Government.
facts.quote: District Collector is an officer belonging to the Indian Administrative Service (IAS). ... While she/he is selected by the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), the appointment is made by the State Government.

facts.text: The Collector maintains law and order, collects land revenue and can implement state and national welfare schemes.
facts.quote: the District Collector is entrusted with the critical responsibilities of maintaining law and order, and collecting land revenue. Furthermore, the District Collector holds the authority to implement various welfare schemes initiated at both the state and national levels.

facts.text: As District Magistrate, the Collector inspects police stations once a year and can impose prohibitionary orders in a law and order crisis.
facts.quote: Inspecting police stations once a year. Functioning in the capacity of District Magistrate. Imposing prohibitionary orders (assembly bans) in the event of a law and order crisis.

facts.text: As District Election Officer, the Collector is Election Officer for Parliamentary and Legislative Assembly elections, updates voter lists, arranges polling security and declares results.
facts.quote: Serving as the Election Officer during Parliamentary and Legislative Assembly elections. Updating the district's voter lists. Ensuring the provision of necessary security arrangements for polling stations. Conducting vote counting and declaring election results.

facts.text: The Collector is ex-officio Chairperson of the District Disaster Management Committee and gives relief to disaster victims.
facts.quote: Serving as the ex-officio Chairperson of the District Disaster Management Committee. Providing relief and rehabilitation to disaster victims.

facts.text: A district's smaller subdivisions are Talukas; the Tehsildar heads the Taluka revenue administration under the direct supervision of the Collector.
facts.quote: A district is constituted by combining various smaller subdivisions; these subdivisions are known as Talukas. Tehsildar serves as the head of the Taluka revenue administration. ... She/He functions under the direct supervision and control of the District Collector.

facts.text: Tehsildar functions: registering and partitioning land titles, collecting land revenue, removing encroachments, disaster relief, issuing certificates, acting as Magistrate in certain civil land cases.
facts.quote: Registering and partitioning land titles. Collecting land revenue. Removing encroachments on land. Participating in disaster management and relief operations. Issuing all important certificates related to civic amenities. Acting as a Magistrate in certain civil cases related to land matters.

facts.text: The Talathi is a village-level Revenue Department employee who collects revenue, recovers 'Tagai' (agricultural) loans, keeps records of immovable property and implements drought relief.
facts.quote: Talathi is a village-level employee of the Revenue Department. ... Collecting revenue and managing and recovering 'Tagai' (agricultural) loans. Maintaining records of the village's immovable properties and issuing extracts thereof. Implementing drought relief measures.

facts.text: The Talathi is under the direct supervision of the 'Mandal Adhikari' (Circle Officer), who reports to the Tehsildar.
facts.quote: The Talathi is under the direct supervision of the 'Mandal Adhikari' (Circle Officer), who, in turn, reports to the Tehsildar.

facts.text: Dr. Rajendra Bharud, then District Collector of Nandurbar, used his medical expertise to set up 'Oxygen Plants' during COVID-19, making Nandurbar self-reliant in oxygen.
facts.quote: To combat the COVID-19 pandemic, Dr. Rajendra Bharud, the then District Collector of Nandurbar, utilized his medical expertise to establish 'Oxygen Plants' Consequently, Nandurbar district became self-reliant in terms of oxygen availability.

facts.text: E. Z. Khobragade (IAS) started 'Reading of the Preamble to the Constitution' in every school across Nagpur district.
facts.quote: E. Z. Khobragade implemented an initiative titled 'Reading of the Preamble to the Constitution' in every school across the Nagpur district, with the objective of fostering awareness about the Constitution.

facts.text: The Government of Maharashtra made reading of the Preamble mandatory in every school in the state from 2008.
facts.quote: Taking cognizance of this initiative, the Government of Maharashtra made reading of the Preamble mandatory in every school across the state starting from the year 2008.

facts.text: Implementing schemes of the Central and State governments is the responsibility of the District Collector.
facts.quote: Responsibility for implementing various schemes of the Central and State governments rests with the District Collector.

facts.text: Social and welfare schemes include 'Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao' and 'Antyodaya'.
facts.quote: Social and Welfare Schemes: ... for instance, 'Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao' scheme, 'Antyodaya' scheme etc.

facts.text: Rural development schemes include Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (Prime Minister's Rural Roads Scheme) and the Rural Livelihood Missions.
facts.quote: For example: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (Prime Minister's Rural Roads Scheme), National and Maharashtra State Rural Livelihood Missions, Chief Minister's Rural Roads Scheme etc.

facts.text: Agriculture-related schemes include Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana (Prime Minister's Agricultural Irrigation Scheme).
facts.quote: Agriculture-related Schemes : ... For example: Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana (Prime Minister's Agricultural Irrigation Scheme) etc.

facts.text: The District Police ensure public safety, maintain law and order and prevent crime.
facts.quote: The primary functions of the District Police machinery include ensuring public safety, maintaining law and order, and preventing crime, among others.

facts.text: The Superintendent of Police heads the district police and is selected through the UPSC.
facts.quote: The head of the police machinery at the district level is the Superintendent of Police, who leads the District Police Force. ... He/She is selected through the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC).

facts.text: 'Sadrakshanaya Khalanigrahanaya' is the motto of the Maharashtra Police Force.
facts.quote: 'Sadrakshanaya Khalanigrahanaya' is the motto of the Maharashtra Police Force.

facts.text: District police ranks: Superintendent, Additional Superintendent, Deputy Superintendent, Police Inspector, Assistant Police Inspector, Sub-Inspector, Assistant Sub-Inspector, Police Head Constable, Police Constable.
facts.quote: 1. Superintendent of Police 2. Additional Superintendent of Police 3. Deputy Superintendent of Police 4. Police Inspector 5. Assistant Police Inspector 6. Sub-Inspector 7. Assistant Sub-Inspector 8. Police Head Constable 9. Police Constable

facts.text: The Superintendent of Police prevents crime, gives the public a sense of security, manages traffic and supports disaster management; VIP security rests with the District Police Administration.
facts.quote: To prevent crime within the district and keep it under control. To instill a sense of security among the general public. To manage traffic. ... Responsibility for the security of Very Important Persons (VIPs) rests with the District Police Administration.

facts.text: Hacking, data misuse, viruses, email fraud, threats or ransom through computers and the internet are called 'cybercrime'; the Cyber Helpline number is 1930.
facts.quote: ... are collectively termed as 'cybercrime'. Cyber Helpline Phone Number: 1930.

facts.text: The District Judge is the principal judicial officer of the district: called 'District Judge' in civil cases and 'Sessions Judge' in criminal cases.
facts.quote: District Judge is the principal judicial officer at the district level. When presiding over civil cases, this officer is designated as the 'District Judge'; while presiding over criminal cases, the designation becomes 'Sessions Judge.'

facts.text: The Judiciary is the guardian of the Constitution; the High Court works under the Supreme Court, and the District Court under the High Court.
facts.quote: Judiciary, or the judicial system, is recognized as the guardian of the Constitution. The High Court functions under the superintendence of the Supreme Court, while the District Court functions under the superintendence of the High Court.

facts.text: The Governor of the State appoints the District Judge on the recommendation of the High Court.
facts.quote: The Governor of the State appoints the District Judge on the recommendation from the High Court.

facts.text: Each district court is headed by a Principal Judge called the 'District and Sessions Judge', helped by subordinate judges; it handles civil and criminal cases.
facts.quote: Each district court is headed by a Principal Judge, who is designated as the 'District and Sessions Judge.' They are assisted in their duties by several subordinate judges. The District Court handles both civil and criminal cases.

facts.text: Court chart: civil - District Judge, Additional District Judge, Civil Judge (Senior Division), Civil Judge (Junior Division); criminal - Sessions Judge, Additional Sessions Judge, Chief Judicial Magistrate, Judicial Magistrate (First Class).
facts.quote: Civil Cases ... District Judge ... Additional District Judge ... Civil Judge (Senior Division) ... Civil Judge (Junior Division); Criminal Cases ... Sessions Judge ... Additional Sessions Judge ... Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate ... Court of Judicial Magistrate (First Class)

facts.text: Civil cases include disputes on ownership, possession and encroachment of land and property, and partition of family property and inheritance.
facts.quote: Civil Cases: a) Adjudicating disputes regarding ownership rights, possession, encroachment etc., concerning land and other property. b) Adjudicating claims related to the partition of family property, inheritance rights etc.

facts.text: Offences punishable by imprisonment exceeding three years, such as dacoity and murder, are tried in the Sessions Court.
facts.quote: All cases involving offenses punishable by imprisonment exceeding three years are tried in the Sessions Court. Examples include serious crimes such as dacoity (armed robbery), murder etc.

facts.text: The District Court is the main appellate court of the district and hears appeals against Civil Judges (Senior Division) and Chief Judicial Magistrates.
facts.quote: District Court serves as the primary appellate court within the district. ... The District Court has the authority to hear appeals filed against judgments of Civil Judges (Senior Division) and Chief Judicial Magistrates.

facts.text: The District Court has full authority over appointment, promotion, transfer and disciplinary action for staff of courts under it.
facts.quote: District Court possesses full authority regarding the appointment, promotion, transfer and disciplinary action concerning the staff of all courts falling under the jurisdiction of the District and Sessions Court.

facts.text: Other district-level courts: Family Court, Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum, Labour / Industrial Court and Juvenile Justice Board.
facts.quote: Other District-Level Courts Family Court Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum Labour / Industrial Court Juvenile Justice Board

facts.text: The Legal Services Authority was established in India in 1987 to provide free legal aid to the weaker sections of society.
facts.quote: The Legal Services Authority was established in India in 1987 with the objective of providing free legal aid to the weaker sections of society.

facts.text: A key objective of the Legal Services Authority is that no citizen is denied justice because of economic or other disabilities.
facts.quote: A key objective of this Legal Services Authority is to ensure that no citizen is denied justice on grounds of economic or other disabilities.
